bluf: Anicca Digital is an independent Leicester agency, founded 2007 with 20+ staff, selling SEO, PPC and paid social to mid market ecommerce and B2B brands and now leading with AI powered marketing, automations and training. The record shows it rebuilding itself for the AI era, with a 2024 AI & Insights launch and edition 3 of its Claude Code Guide in May 2026. The Horus read rates it Favored at 20.4, best placed for the hollowing of the agency middle. A rival should know its own house contradicts two sold lines: no llms.txt behind the AI visibility offer and no social pixel behind paid social.
doing:
The positioning line reads: independent Leicester agency since 2007 offering AI powered marketing and growth for ecommerce and B2B brands, plus bespoke AI solutions, dashboards, automations and training. In plain words: a search and paid media shop with an AI consultancy and training arm bolted on. The headline claim stacks proof: a 4.87 average across 700 reviews.io reviews, 19 years independent, Google Premier Partner status and 4,000+ marketers trained.

The services list adds Shopping, digital PR, affiliate marketing, AI discovery workshops and reporting dashboards to the channel lines. The lead lines, each at 3, are AI Automation / Agents (the H1 sells AI powered marketing; the AI & Insights arm offers automations and C4), Paid Search (the title names PPC; a custom Google Ads labelling script for Big Furniture Warehouse) and SEO (the homepage title leads with SEO; case studies for GB DIY, Trifibre and Charles Bentley). Core lines at 2 are AI Search / GEO (a free GEO audit benchmarks visibility in AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude), Data & Measurement (bespoke dashboards in the hero) and Paid Social (a Meta ecommerce case for the Irish retailer EZ Living Furniture). Proprietary names: C10 Framework, C4 (Company Command & Control Centre), Thursday AI Club and The Claude Code Guide; the one partner listed is Google Premier Partner.

The AI posture is explicit: rebuilding the agency for the AI era, with weekly AI in Marketing & Management news roundups behind it.

Moves in date order: in 2024 it launched Anicca AI & Insights (workshops, bespoke solutions, dashboards, automations, training); in May 2026 it released edition 3 of its Claude Code Guide. Pricing signals are thin: a Pricing & Rate Card page (rates not captured), subscription SaaS for marketers and agencies, and a free audit offer. Conspicuously absent for an ecommerce growth shop: CRO, email and CRM, web and retail media all at 0; no jobs, news or captured awards.
clients:
The Radar files the client type as mid market, the verticals as Ecommerce & retail, Furniture & homeware, DIY & building products, B2B manufacturing and Property, and the home market as Leicester and the wider United Kingdom, with one Irish retailer on the books. The needs read counts 7 clients, all case studies: 3 observed and 4 named only.

The observed needs are organic and paid. Charles Bentley came for organic demand (case study slug: organic visibility increase) and so did GB DIY (slug: seo); EZ Living Furniture came for paid performance (slug: paid media), a Meta ecommerce strategy per the capability note. Big Furniture Warehouse, Trifibre, Honey Brothers and Europlaz are named only in the needs read, though the capability notes add detail for two of them, a custom Google Ads labelling script for Big Furniture Warehouse and SEO work for Trifibre, so those read as paid performance and organic demand; the needs of Honey Brothers and Europlaz are inferred from the sold mix, search and paid media.

The mix read is organic demand at 0.667 and paid performance at 0.333, with no AI or automation need observed on any client despite the AI lead line. No client is shared with another tracked agency (shared count 0). Most of the book is names only (4 of 7).

What the base needs next: the edition's KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) are its tailwinds, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that its furniture, DIY and manufacturing clients will be sold AI visibility audits and automation on top of search retainers; the record shows the offer (the free GEO audit) but no client case for it yet.
house: Say and do: 3 of 5 tested lines are practised. Paid search is corroborated (it runs its own Google ads, 2 in the Transparency Center, 0 in the last 30 days, last shown 20 January 2026), LinkedIn advertising is corroborated (21 company page ads) and publishing cadence is corroborated (72 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, 124 in 365, from a sitemap of 309). AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while 13 AI topic URLs sit in its sitemap. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. The tag stack is GTM and GA4 on WordPress with Elementor; no test tools or ABM stack are listed; no AI crawler is blocked. The LinkedIn samples sell the training arm; one reads that generative AI and AI agents are no longer a competitive advantage, they are fast becoming a baseline capability.
market:
The Horus read scores a tailwind index of 20.4, Favored band. It is best placed for KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net 0.298), driven by AI Automation / Agents, and for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.257), driven by AI Search / GEO. It is most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer, net -0.154) through Paid Search and Paid Social. Best fit is The Bazaar of Agents at 50/100. The read has it making P1 (an audited AI visibility product), P4 (inputs for automation) and P6 (agent operators, with an AI upskilling programme), unknown on P5, and absent on P2, P7 and P8.

The Monsoon read scores 55.9, Onshore wind band: migration 53.4 against displacement 58.4, with SEO (16) and Paid Search (11) carrying the most movable hours and automation overlapping 28% of them. The work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia, 20% to Eastern Europe and 15% to Africa and the Maghreb. No hub office and no onshore claim are listed, footprint inferred.
openings:
Lead with the contradictions. It sells AI visibility and publishes 13 AI topic URLs, yet has no llms.txt; it sells paid social and runs no social pixel. A rival whose house passes both tests can put the gap on one slide; very likely, high confidence, it lands with ecommerce clients buying GEO on trust. The falsifier is an llms.txt and a social pixel appearing on anicca.co.uk.

The furniture book is contestable on paid: Big Furniture Warehouse and EZ Living Furniture are paid clients, KJ4 exposure runs through Paid Search and Paid Social, and no ads are tested inside AI assistants (P8 absent); an agency showing assistant ad results with holdouts likely sets the price, moderate confidence.

The machine readable layer is unclaimed: SEO is a lead line and the record shows no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent), so a feeds and entities offer undercuts its GEO audit. Pricing is soft: rates on its rate card page were not captured (P5 unknown), so a public outcome priced offer forces a conversation it has not had. The AI training arm is unlikely to be contestable on price alone: 4,000+ marketers trained and 21 LinkedIn ads show a working funnel.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would strengthen its KJ6 tailwind.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalisation of the search retainers it leads with, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1.

I10, Reddit US daily users versus search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind its KJ1 tailwind.

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the next milestone ($2B) and its timing, with pricing below $20 CPM signalling supply outrunning demand in the assistant ad market it has not tested.
The May 2026 release of edition 3 of the Claude Code Guide: a further edition or a paid course would show the training arm scaling beyond the 4,000+ claim.
The next Radar compile: the dossier is only as fresh as 28 September 2026, and a new compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients.
